Verified 2026-08-08 by installing all three profiles into temp consumers and listing the

renders: landing site /docs/installation/ — human render (getff-ai-site S1; the first-steps-* quick-start slugs are stubs per face spec §4, so the render target is the Installation page — BU-F14 re-point, S0a)

core.goal: install -> a rule provably fires on your code
core.profileFlag: --profile core (core is never the default — install.sh:648 makes the non-interactive default `env`)

steps.title: Install at core depth
steps.action: From your project root run `bash <getff>/setup -y --profile core <stack>` — `core` must be named, because `-y` on its own resolves to `env` (install.sh:648). (stacks: ts-server, react-next, react-spa, react-native; `python`, `cargo` and `go` are separate non-npm toolchain lanes, each an explicit positional — `./setup cargo` or `bash install.sh cargo`, the wrapper forwards lanes verbatim). Omit the stack to auto-detect.

steps.title: Verify the payload landed
steps.action: `ls AGENTS.md .ai-factory/ scripts/` — you should see AGENTS.md, `.ai-factory/{DESCRIPTION.md,ARCHITECTURE.md,RULES.md}` and `scripts/audit-ai-docs.sh`. Nothing here is optional; a missing file means the install did not finish.

steps.title: Fill the project passport
steps.action: Replace every `<PLACEHOLDER>` in `.ai-factory/DESCRIPTION.md` (domain, stack, constraints, non-goals). This is the file AGENTS.md sends every future session to first, so a passport left unfilled degrades every later session.

steps.title: Prove the rules are not inert on your layout
steps.action: `bash scripts/check-rule-globs.sh` — fails when a shipped custom rule matches ZERO files in your layout, i.e. it is installed but silently enforcing nothing. If it fires, widen `RULE_GLOBS` in `eslint.config.mjs` to cover your layout. On a brand-new skeleton with no source files yet this FAILS by design — every rule matches zero files. That is the expected first run; re-run it once your first `src/` files exist.
steps.evidence: scripts/check-rule-globs.sh (shipped at core; verified in a temp consumer 2026-08-08)

steps.title: Watch a rule actually fire
steps.action: `bash scripts/check-fences-fire.sh` — plants deliberately-bad input in a temp dir and asserts the installed ESLint rules go RED on it. This is the first-rule-fires moment: an installed rule that has never been seen to fire is an unproven claim.

steps.title: Fire a rule on YOUR code, not a fixture
steps.action: Plant one violation of a shipped getff rule in YOUR tree and run your stack's native gate — the RED line names your file. npm: add `z.string().parse(input)` to a file under a boundary glob (`**/routes/**`, `**/handlers/**`, `**/controllers/**`, `**/app/api/**`, `**/actions/**`), run `npm run lint` — RED from `rules-as-tests/no-unsafe-zod-parse` (R2, the one custom rule wired unconditionally; R7/R8 fire only under `AIF_STRICT_RUNTIME=1`). Lanes: python — add `datetime.utcnow()`, run `ruff check . --config .getff/ruff-bans.toml`; cargo — add `std::env::var("X")`, run `cargo clippy`; go — add `os.Getenv("X")`, run `golangci-lint run`.
steps.evidence: templates/ts-server/eslint.config.mjs:179 (R2 unconditional); setup.d/70-deps.sh:75 (npm run lint); setup.d/45-python.sh:587 / 46-cargo.sh:256 / 47-go.sh:252 (lane firing self-checks)

steps.title: Run the gate you will run every day
steps.action: `bash scripts/audit-ai-docs.sh` — drift + code-vs-docs probes (~10 sec). Expect findings on a fresh project; the INSTALL-FOR-AI «Expected first-run failures» table lists which ones are normal.

steps.title: Continue into rule research in the same session
steps.action: Invoke `/rule-research` (or read `.claude/agents/rule-researcher.md` on a harness without skills). The installer delivered a curated starter set; researching stack-specific rules from live documentation is the next step of the same lifecycle, not a later project.

env.goal: core + the multi-model contour surface: tier criteria on disk and one idea through /arch

steps.title: Install at env depth
steps.action: `bash <getff>/install.sh <stack> --profile env`. Already on core? Re-run that same command — the deeper payload is added and every core artefact stays byte-identical except `.prettierignore`, whose managed block gains the new paths. Do not reach for `--refresh` to upgrade: it re-delivers fixes to what you already have and does not reliably deepen an install — on a `core` project `--refresh --profile env` exits 0 while `tier-home.md` and `.claude/skills/arch/` stay absent.
steps.evidence: install.sh:1342-1350 — the tier-home refresh arm is presence-gated («refresh must not create it on core»); `arch` is in no do_refresh skill loop. Measured on a core consumer against staging 2026-08-09: `--refresh --profile env` → exit 0, tier-home NO, arch NO (the worktree-scripts arm at install.sh:1251-1256 was ungated and delivered 4 env-tier scripts on a core project; it has carried the env|factory|presence gate since #1334, so that depth-boundary defect is closed); plain `--profile env` → exit 0, tier-home YES, arch YES, every pre-existing core file byte-identical except .prettierignore. Also INSTALL-FOR-AI.md «Install depth profiles»

steps.title: Verify the payload landed
steps.action: `ls AGENTS.md .ai-factory/ scripts/` plus `.ai-factory/tier-home.md` and the five skills env adds over core: `.claude/skills/arch/`, `.claude/skills/night-mode/`, `.claude/skills/orchestrator/`, `.claude/skills/pipeline/` and `.claude/skills/reviewer/`.
steps.evidence: setup.d/30-templates.sh (tier-home at env+); verified in a temp consumer 2026-08-08

steps.title: Fill the project passport
steps.action: Replace every `<PLACEHOLDER>` in `.ai-factory/DESCRIPTION.md`.

steps.title: Prove the rules are not inert on your layout
steps.action: `bash scripts/check-rule-globs.sh`, then `bash scripts/check-fences-fire.sh` to see a rule go RED on planted input. On a brand-new skeleton with no source files yet this FAILS by design — every rule matches zero files. That is the expected first run; re-run it once your first `src/` files exist.

steps.title: Read the tier + degradation SSOT
steps.action: Open `.ai-factory/tier-home.md`. It owns the Tier 0/1/2 routing criteria and the capability-absence degradation matrix — what still works when there is no aif runtime, no executor-tier model, or a non-Claude-Code harness. AGENTS.md only points here; the criteria live in this one file.

steps.title: Take one idea through `/arch`
steps.action: Invoke `/arch <topic>` — the external design contour turns a raw idea into a reviewed design plus a routed handoff. On a harness without skills, read `.claude/skills/arch/SKILL.md` and follow it by hand.
steps.evidence: .claude/skills/arch/SKILL.md (shipped at env+; verified in a temp consumer 2026-08-08)

factory.goal: env + one task driven through the pipeline

steps.title: Install at factory depth
steps.action: `bash <getff>/install.sh <stack> --profile factory`. Pick this ONLY if this machine runs the aif-handoff operator runtime — the factory payload dead-ends without it.

steps.title: Verify the payload landed
steps.action: `ls .claude/skills/` — on top of env you should see `.claude/skills/dispatcher/`, `.claude/skills/aif-doctor/`, `.claude/skills/harvest/`, `.claude/skills/story/` and `.claude/skills/claude-glm-executor-handoff/`. `pipeline` and `night-mode` are NOT factory additions — they arrive with env+ and are already there.
steps.evidence: setup.d/10-skills.sh; verified in a temp consumer 2026-08-08

steps.title: Fill the project passport
steps.action: Replace every `<PLACEHOLDER>` in `.ai-factory/DESCRIPTION.md`.

steps.title: Prove the rules are not inert on your layout
steps.action: `bash scripts/check-rule-globs.sh`, then `bash scripts/check-fences-fire.sh` to see a rule go RED on planted input. On a brand-new skeleton with no source files yet this FAILS by design — every rule matches zero files. That is the expected first run; re-run it once your first `src/` files exist.

steps.title: Read the tier + degradation SSOT
steps.action: Open `.ai-factory/tier-home.md` — it decides which tier a task routes to, and what degrades when a capability is absent.

steps.title: Write your first kickoff
steps.action: Create `.ai-factory/orchestrator-prompts/<work-item>/kickoff.md`: a `Type:` line (`fix` / `research` / `feature`), the goal, and — if the work splits into parallel sub-steps — a `## §1 Sub-wave` section with one table row per sub-step.

steps.title: Ask the pipeline what to start next
steps.action: Invoke `/pipeline`. It reads your kickoffs plus `.ai-factory/orchestrator-prompts/plan.md` (created on first run), ranks them, and emits a launch table. An empty backlog reports «nothing queued» — that is normal, not an error.
steps.evidence: .claude/skills/pipeline/SKILL.md (shipped at env+; verified in a temp consumer 2026-08-08)

steps.title: Dispatch the top row and read the result
steps.action: Dispatch the launch table's top row, then bring the finished branch back with `/harvest`. If a task stalls or the runtime misbehaves, `/aif-doctor` is the diagnostic entry point.

road.goal: one agent session walks one ordered list from install to its own final report
_note: The install prompt in INSTALL-FOR-AI.md renders this list as lines `N. [id] title`; the parity
fixture compares ids and titles in order. A step that is not built yet stays in the list and
is reported «not done» with a reason, so the report never hides it.

steps.title: Check the installer's prerequisites
steps.action: Confirm git is initialized in this project and the getff checkout from Step 0 exists. On an npm project also confirm Node.js 22.23+ and npm: the installer needs them, the project itself does not have to.
steps.doneTest: `git rev-parse --git-dir` exits 0 and `<getff>/setup` exists; on an npm project `node --version` prints 22.23 or newer

steps.title: Preview the stack and the tool list
steps.action: From the project's directory run `bash <getff>/setup --dry-run`. It writes nothing. Read from its output the stack, the «✓» lines under «Stack-aware companion selection», the «Companions» section and the lines that end «not chosen in the pre-launch list». The stack is the word the installer prints: one of its named stacks, or `generic` for a project it has no stack for. The «✓» lines name every tool the install will handle, MCP servers included; the «Companions» section leaves MCP servers out. Run no probe of your own.
steps.doneTest: the command exits 0, its output names the stack, and `git status --short` of the project is unchanged

steps.title: Ask the ONE question
steps.action: Show the stack, what goes into the project and what would go machine-wide, then ask once, as one list of four parts: (a) where to install — 1, 2 or 3, it picks the installer flag; (b) session settings, yes or no — `GETFF_SESSION_SETTINGS=1` goes before the installer command unless the answer says no; before asking, name the groups the dry run printed and say in plain words: they go into the person's own uncommitted `.claude/settings.local.json`; values the person already set are kept; the handoff gate holds a turn shortly before the conversation is compacted until the session's handoff note is current; the deny list makes the agent refuse commands such as `git reset --hard`, `rm -rf` and `sudo`; the install prints one undo command; (c) tools for the project's own dependencies, yes or no — `GETFF_STACK_TOOLS=1` goes before the installer command unless the answer says no; the installer's own source check decides which servers are taken; (d) research, yes or no. A part the answer leaves out reads: (a) 1, (b) yes, (c) yes, (d) yes — so the answer «1» means everything on, this project only. Nothing else is asked during the run.
steps.doneTest: exactly one question was asked before the installer ran, and the report quotes the answer with the flag and the variables it chose

steps.title: Run the installer with the chosen flag
steps.action: Answer 1: `bash <getff>/setup -y <stack>`. Answer 2: `bash <getff>/setup -y --global <stack>`. Answer 3: `bash <getff>/setup --all <stack>`. Put the variables before the command, on the same line: with no «no» in the answer it reads `GETFF_SESSION_SETTINGS=1 GETFF_STACK_TOOLS=1 bash <getff>/setup -y <stack>`; a «no» drops its variable. Keep the «Checked by the install» block and every «NOT wired» line for the report.
steps.doneTest: the installer exits 0 and prints its «Checked by the install» block

steps.title: Verify the payload landed
steps.action: `ls AGENTS.md .ai-factory/ scripts/ .claude/agents/ .claude/skills/` — a missing entry means the install did not finish.

steps.title: Draft the project passport
steps.action: When `.ai-factory/DESCRIPTION.md` is byte-identical to `.ai-factory/DESCRIPTION.template.md`, draft it from the project's own files by following `.claude/agents/aif-init.md`, marking every guess `[GUESSED — verify]`. A passport the project already had is kept as it is. The run never waits for a human here.
steps.doneTest: `.ai-factory/DESCRIPTION.md` differs from the template and holds none of the template's `<…>` placeholder tokens

steps.title: Check that everything getff uses for itself is installed or marked
steps.action: Take the tool names from the «✓ <name>» lines the preview printed under «Stack-aware companion selection», leave out the external services runtime-bridge and aif-handoff, and add context7. For each of these tools find the one trace the install left, in two sources only: a row `| <name> |` in the `<!-- getff:installed-versions:begin -->` block of `.ai-factory/tool-decisions.md`; or a line `- <name> — <reason>` in the installer's NOT-wired summary or in its kept-values summary. Quote that row or line per tool. A row whose version starts «not read:» is a trace: quote its reason. A tool with no trace is a finding under this step, named «MISSING <name>». Run no probe of your own. When the block is absent, report this step as «not done: no installed-versions record in tool-decisions.md» and go on.
steps.doneTest: the block exists and every selected tool has its row or its summary line; each tool without one is named MISSING

steps.title: Read the base-core list with a status per principle
steps.action: Read the table in `.claude/skills/getff/references/base-core.md`; change nothing. Every row whose status is not `fires`, and every row whose «not on stack» column names this project's stack, goes into the report section «PRINCIPLES NOT WIRED YET» as one line: id, principle, status, reason. When the file is absent, report this step as «not done: list absent in this older install» and put one yes-or-no decision into «WHAT I NEED FROM YOU»: refresh getff's own files in this project.
steps.doneTest: the count of lines in «PRINCIPLES NOT WIRED YET» equals the count of such rows in the file

steps.title: Research rules for the stack
steps.action: Unless the answer to the one question said no to research, follow `<getff>/agents/rule-researcher.md`; it has an arm per toolchain. The answer to the one question is the confirmation that protocol asks for: write its files without asking, and list what was written in the report. Report where it ended.
steps.doneTest: the rule-research sequence reached its own completion output, or the report names the point where it stopped

steps.title: Write one rule table and place each rule in its home
steps.action: After the research step, run `bash <getff>/setup --full <stack>` with the same variables before it that the install step passed — a run without them reports the choices of the one answer as not chosen: the installer places each rule in the project's own linter. Then run `node scripts/prove-rules.mjs --prove` once and quote its table; the same output serves the next step. When `scripts/prove-rules.mjs` is absent after the installer ran, report this step as «not done: scripts/prove-rules.mjs absent in this install» and go on.
steps.doneTest: the table prints one row per rule

steps.title: Prove the placed rules in one batch run
steps.action: Read the proof from the output the previous step already produced; do not run it again. Quote the proof line and the exit code. A rule that fails its proof is a finding under this step and stays in place. When the previous step is «not done», report this step as «not done» with the same reason.
steps.doneTest: the proof line shows bad→exit ≠0, good→exit 0

steps.title: Run the project's own check commands as the installer wired them
steps.action: Run each command listed under `armed:` in the block `<!-- aif:project-checks:begin -->` of `.ai-factory/tool-decisions.md`. Quote exit codes and failing lines, then the lines under `not-armed:` with their reasons; failures on the project's existing code are a finding, not a reason to stop. When the block is absent, report «not done: no check record in tool-decisions.md»; when nothing is listed under `armed:`, report «not done: no check armed».
steps.doneTest: each armed command ran and its exit code is in the report

steps.title: Print the final report
steps.action: Print the report in the format given with the prompt: one line per step of this list, in order, none omitted.
steps.doneTest: the report carries exactly one line per step id, each reading «done» with a check command or «not done» with a reason
